paragraphs.title: Longing for God and a Request for Guidance

easy.explanation: Verse 1 says, “Unto thee, O LORD, do I lift up my soul.”
easy.q: Unto whom does the psalmist lift up his soul?

easy.explanation: Verse 2 says, “O my God, I trust in thee.”
easy.q: In whom does the psalmist trust?

easy.explanation: Verse 4 says, “Shew me thy ways, O LORD.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to show him?

answers: Because he trusts in the LORD
Because he wants to boast in himself
Because he does not know the LORD
medium.explanation: His request not to be ashamed follows his declaration, “I trust in thee.”
medium.q: Why does the psalmist ask not to be ashamed?

answers: To hope and patiently depend on the LORD
medium.explanation: The psalmist says he waits on God and looks to Him for salvation.
medium.q: What does “wait on thee” mean in this passage?

medium.explanation: Verses 4–5 ask God to teach His paths and lead the psalmist in His truth.
medium.q: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to teach him?

answers: Because he trusts God, the psalmist seeks to learn and follow God’s ways
Trust causes him to reject God’s instruction
challenge.explanation: The psalmist’s trust leads him to ask God to guide and teach him.
challenge.q: What connection exists between trusting the LORD and asking for guidance?

answers: A strong desire to live according to God’s will
A desire to avoid the truth
challenge.explanation: The repeated requests show the psalmist’s longing for God’s direction.
challenge.q: What does the repeated language of teaching and leading in verses 4–5 emphasize?

challenge.explanation: Verse 5 says, “on thee do I wait all the day.”
challenge.q: What is the basis of the psalmist’s hope throughout the day?

paragraphs.title: God’s Compassion and Forgiveness of Sin

easy.explanation: Verse 6 asks God to remember His tender mercies and lovingkindnesses.
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to remember?

answers: The sins of his youth and his transgressions
Only the sins of his enemies
easy.explanation: Verse 7 says, “Remember not the sins of my youth, nor my transgressions.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask God not to remember?

easy.explanation: Verses 8–9 say that the LORD teaches sinners and guides the meek.
easy.q: Whom does the LORD teach in the way?

answers: His iniquity, because it is great
medium.explanation: Verse 11 says, “pardon mine iniquity; for it is great.”
medium.q: For what does the psalmist ask pardon?

answers: Humble people who are willing to receive God’s instruction
medium.explanation: The meek are described as those whom God guides and teaches.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “the meek” describe?

answers: His way and the right path
medium.explanation: God teaches sinners in the way and teaches the meek His way.
medium.q: What does the LORD teach sinners and the meek?

answers: For the LORD’s name’s sake and according to His goodness
So that he may boast in himself
So that he may turn away from God
challenge.explanation: Verse 11 appeals to the LORD’s name and goodness as the basis for pardon.
challenge.q: According to these verses, why does the psalmist ask for pardon?

challenge.explanation: Verse 10 says, “All the paths of the LORD are mercy and truth.”
challenge.q: Which pair describes all the paths of the LORD in verse 10?

answers: His goodness is shown by teaching them the right way
His goodness causes Him to hide the way
His goodness has no connection with guidance
challenge.explanation: Verse 8 connects the LORD’s goodness and uprightness with teaching sinners.
challenge.q: How is God’s goodness connected with His teaching sinners?

paragraphs.title: The Path and Blessing of Those Who Fear God

answers: Instruction in the way he should choose
easy.explanation: Verse 12 says the LORD teaches the person who fears Him in the way he shall choose.
easy.q: What does the person who fears the LORD receive?

easy.explanation: Verse 13 says, “His soul shall dwell at ease.”
easy.q: In what condition shall the soul of the one who fears the LORD dwell?

easy.explanation: Verse 15 says the LORD will pluck his feet out of the net.
easy.q: What does the LORD pluck the psalmist’s feet out of?

answers: To honor God and be willing to follow His direction
To refuse to hope in God
medium.explanation: The person who fears the LORD receives God’s teaching and guidance.
medium.q: What does it mean in this passage to fear the LORD?

answers: His seed shall inherit the earth
His seed shall have no hope
His seed shall flee from the land
medium.explanation: Verse 13 says, “his seed shall inherit the earth.”
medium.q: What is promised concerning the seed of the one who fears the LORD?

answers: The LORD’s close counsel and revealed covenant
medium.explanation: Verse 14 says the secret of the LORD is with those who fear Him, and He shows them His covenant.
medium.q: What does “the secret of the LORD” refer to in this passage?

answers: The person who fears the LORD is willing to receive His instruction
The person who fears the LORD refuses all guidance
Fear of the LORD prevents a person from seeking Him
challenge.explanation: Verse 12 presents the one who fears the LORD as someone whom God teaches.
challenge.q: What connection exists between fearing the LORD and receiving guidance?

answers: Continual dependence on God for help
That the psalmist has forgotten God
That the psalmist trusts only his enemies
challenge.explanation: The psalmist continually looks to the LORD because he expects Him to rescue him.
challenge.q: What does the statement “Mine eyes are ever toward the LORD” reveal?

answers: The person who fears God receives instruction, learns of His covenant, and looks to Him for rescue
They are presented as contradictory ideas
challenge.explanation: The verses join God’s guidance and covenant relationship with His power to deliver from danger.
challenge.q: How do guidance, covenant, and deliverance relate in these verses?

paragraphs.title: A Cry from Loneliness, Distress, and Enemies

easy.explanation: Verse 16 says, “I am desolate and afflicted.”
easy.q: How does the psalmist describe himself?

answers: Turn toward him and have mercy
easy.explanation: Verse 16 says, “Turn thee unto me, and have mercy upon me.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to do toward him?

easy.explanation: He asks God to bring him out of his distresses and protect him from his enemies.
easy.q: From what does the psalmist seek deliverance?

medium.explanation: Verse 17 says, “The troubles of my heart are enlarged.”
medium.q: What caused the psalmist’s distress to increase?

medium.explanation: The word describes the troubles and hardships from which he asks to be delivered.
medium.q: What does “my distresses” mean in this passage?

answers: That God forgive all his sins
medium.q: After asking God to look upon his affliction and pain, what does the psalmist ask?

answers: They cause him to ask the LORD for mercy and deliverance
They cause him to stop hoping
They cause him to praise his enemies
challenge.explanation: Because he is desolate and afflicted, he turns to God for mercy and rescue.
challenge.q: How do loneliness and distress shape the psalmist’s prayer?

answers: He seeks help for both his inward sins and outward troubles
He refuses to acknowledge his condition
challenge.explanation: The prayer addresses both sin and the difficult circumstances surrounding him.
challenge.q: What can be learned from the psalmist asking for both forgiveness and deliverance?

answers: The seriousness of the threat and the need for God’s protection
challenge.explanation: Their number and cruel hatred make the danger especially severe.
challenge.q: What does the description of the enemies as many and cruel emphasize?

easy.explanation: Verse 21 says, “Let integrity and uprightness preserve me.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask to preserve him?

easy.explanation: The verse ends with, “for I wait on thee.”
easy.q: In whom does the psalmist place his hope?

answers: Trust in integrity and the LORD
A description of a geographical path
easy.explanation: The verse joins integrity and uprightness with waiting on the LORD.
easy.q: What is the main subject of this verse?

medium.explanation: Integrity is presented alongside uprightness as a quality of righteous conduct.
medium.q: What does “integrity” mean in this verse?

answers: Because he waits on the LORD
Because he does not want protection
medium.explanation: The word “for” connects his request with his waiting on the LORD.
medium.q: Why does the psalmist ask integrity and uprightness to preserve him?

answers: Integrity and uprightness are presented as preserving influences
They are presented as sources of danger
medium.explanation: The psalmist directly asks that integrity and uprightness preserve him.
medium.q: What relationship does the verse show between integrity and preservation?

answers: He emphasizes righteous character and dependence on God
He boasts in his military strength
challenge.explanation: The verse points to moral character and trust in God rather than human force.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the psalmist asking for preservation through integrity rather than military power?

answers: The psalmist still places his hope in the LORD
He has stopped trusting the LORD
He turns only to his enemies
challenge.explanation: Waiting on the LORD continues the psalm’s repeated theme of dependence on Him.
challenge.q: How does this verse continue the theme of trust found earlier in the psalm?

answers: They appear together as a righteous way of life grounded in trust
They have no connection with prayer
challenge.explanation: The verse presents moral character and hope in God as closely connected.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between integrity, uprightness, and waiting on the LORD?

easy.q: Whom does the psalmist ask God to redeem?

easy.explanation: The verse asks God to redeem Israel “out of all his troubles.”
easy.q: From what does the psalmist ask God to redeem Israel?

easy.explanation: The final verse expands the prayer from the individual to Israel as a whole.
easy.q: To whom does the prayer extend at the end of the psalm?

medium.explanation: Here, redemption means delivering Israel from all its troubles.
medium.q: What does “redeem” mean in this verse?

medium.explanation: The verse uses the phrase “out of all his troubles.”
medium.q: How extensive is the trouble from which Israel needs deliverance?

answers: It moves from the individual psalmist to all Israel
It moves from Israel to the enemies
It moves from deliverance to wealth
medium.explanation: The final petition concerns the redemption of the entire nation.
medium.q: How does the focus of the prayer change in the final verse?

answers: Hope and salvation concern both the individual and the community
The psalmist rejects concern for the nation
The psalm is only about enemies
challenge.explanation: The conclusion broadens the personal prayer into a prayer for the whole people.
challenge.q: What may be inferred from placing the request for Israel’s redemption at the end of the psalm?

answers: It extends the request for deliverance from the psalmist’s troubles to Israel’s troubles
It removes the subject of trouble
challenge.explanation: The final verse asks for Israel to be delivered from all its troubles.
challenge.q: How is the request for Israel’s redemption connected with the theme of trouble in the psalm?

answers: A complete deliverance from every trouble
A partial deliverance from one trouble
challenge.explanation: The word “all” makes the request comprehensive rather than limited.
challenge.q: What does the word “all” emphasize in the request?
